name: DevOps Engineer Roadmap
tagline: From the shell to running fleets of containers you can observe, scale and recover
summary: An ordered path for engineers who build and run the platform other developers deploy onto. It starts with Linux, scripting and Git, then the networking layers every outage eventually traces back to, then containers, pipelines and infrastructure as code, and finally the orchestration, observability and reliability practices that keep production up while it changes many times a day.

steps.label: Linux & the shell
steps.note: Every server, container and CI runner is Linux; processes, permissions, file descriptors, ports and systemd are the vocabulary of every incident.

steps.label: Scripting (Bash & Python)
steps.note: Automation is the job; a glue language for parsing logs, calling APIs and wiring tools together comes before any specific tool.

steps.label: Git & version control
steps.note: Infrastructure, pipelines and configuration all live in Git; branching, reviews and history are how change is controlled later.

steps.label: TCP/IP & networking basics
steps.note: Connections, ports, retransmits and timeouts explain the 'it works locally but times out in the cluster' class of problems.

steps.label: DNS
steps.note: Service discovery, TTL-driven failover and half of all 'the site is down' reports are DNS; learn it before load balancers depend on it.

steps.label: TLS & certificates
steps.note: Terminating, rotating and trusting certificates is a platform responsibility, and expired certs are a classic self-inflicted outage.

steps.label: HTTP
steps.note: Health checks, proxies, caches and gateways all speak HTTP; status codes and headers are how you read what a proxy did to a request.

steps.label: Nginx & reverse proxies
steps.note: A reverse proxy is the first place TLS, routing, compression and rate limits meet real traffic — and the simplest load balancer you will run.

steps.label: Load balancing
steps.note: Once traffic spans several instances, algorithms, health checks and connection draining decide whether a deploy is invisible or an outage.

steps.label: Docker & containers
steps.note: Images, layers, namespaces and cgroups are the unit everything downstream schedules; build small, reproducible images before orchestrating them.

steps.label: CI/CD pipelines
steps.note: Automated build, test and deploy on every push turns container images into a repeatable delivery flow and removes hand-run deploy scripts.

steps.label: Infrastructure as Code (Terraform)
steps.note: Declaring networks, clusters and databases in reviewed code makes environments reproducible and destroys the snowflake server.

steps.label: Cloud platforms (AWS / GCP / Azure)
steps.note: IAM, VPCs, managed databases and object storage are the primitives Terraform provisions; know one provider's model deeply.

steps.label: Object storage
steps.note: Artifacts, backups, logs and Terraform state all land in object storage; its consistency and cost model shape how you use it.

steps.label: Kubernetes
steps.note: With containers, networking and cloud primitives understood, the orchestrator's scheduling, rollouts, probes and autoscaling stop being magic.

steps.label: Secrets & configuration management
steps.note: Credentials and config must be injected, rotated and audited outside images; this is where platform and security teams meet.

steps.label: Prometheus & metrics
steps.note: Pull-based metrics, labels and alert rules are how you know a rollout is failing before users tell you.

steps.label: Observability (logs, metrics, traces)
steps.note: Metrics say something is wrong, logs and traces say where; correlating the three across services is the skill that shortens incidents.

steps.label: Availability & SLOs
steps.note: Defining error budgets and SLOs turns 'is it reliable enough' into a number that decides when to ship and when to harden.

steps.label: Resilience patterns
steps.note: Timeouts, retries with backoff, circuit breakers and bulkheads are how a platform stops one failing dependency from taking down the rest.

steps.label: Incident response & postmortems
steps.note: On-call rotations, runbooks and blameless postmortems convert outages into fixes; this is where the previous steps prove their worth.

steps.label: Platform for microservices
steps.note: Finish by studying a microservices architecture end to end — gateway, discovery, messaging, observability — and mapping each part to what you now run.
